concepts.why: The patient has lymphoblasts, low hemoglobin, low white-cell count, and low platelets, which are all indicative of acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
The patient has febrile neutropenia, which is a common complication of chemotherapy.
The patient has eczematous plaques on her chest and proximal right arm, which were treated as contact dermatitis.
The patient has severe pain in her right arm radiating to her shoulder, and an MRI showed a focal cystic necrotic lesion, which is consistent with herpes zoster.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's laboratory results, including low hemoglobin, white-cell count, and platelets, along with the presence of lymphoblasts, strongly support the diagnosis of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia, which explains the decisive findings without unexplained strong contradictions.
